title: Data Analyst
summary: Turn raw data into decisions: SQL, Python, pandas, cleaning, visualization, statistics and a dashboard you can present.

nodes.title: Data Thinking
nodes.description: What analysis is actually for: questions, datasets, sources and what 'good data' means.

tasks.title: Kaggle Learn: data analysis
tasks.description: Kaggle's free beginner course on data analysis and Python.

tasks.title: FreeCodeCamp data analysis intro
tasks.description: Watch an introduction to the analyst workflow: question → data → insight → decision.

tasks.title: Frame 3 real problems as data questions
tasks.description: Pick three decisions from your own life (or a job ad you like) and write each as a precise, answerable data question. Note which data you would need.

nodes.title: CSVs & Spreadsheets
nodes.description: Work with the format every dataset arrives in: reading, sorting, filtering and pivoting tables.

tasks.title: Google Sheets help
tasks.description: The official Sheets help docs: formulas, sorting and filtering basics.

tasks.title: Clean a messy CSV
tasks.description: Find a public CSV (city open data works well). Fix at least: one date column, one number stored as text, and one column with inconsistent casing.

tasks.title: Pivot: totals by group
tasks.description: From any table with a category column and an amount column, build a summary of totals per category using formulas (no macros).

nodes.title: SQL Basics
nodes.description: The analyst's core tool: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and reading tables like a map.

tasks.title: Kaggle Learn: SQL
tasks.description: Kaggle's interactive SQL course — the fastest path from zero to querying real tables.

tasks.title: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
tasks.description: Against any public dataset (Kaggle notebooks have plenty), write three queries: top 10 by one metric, rows matching a condition, and the distinct values of a category column.

tasks.title: SQL basics quiz
tasks.description: Filtering, aggregating and counting.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters rows BEFORE any aggregation happens?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows first; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.prompt: In a grouped query, COUNT(*) counts…
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) tallies every row that falls into the group; COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts unique values.

questions.prompt: Which function returns the average of a column?
questions.explanation: AVG() computes the mean of non-null values; SQL has no MEAN() function.

nodes.title: Python for Data
nodes.description: The analyst's scripting language: variables, loops, dicts and list comprehensions.

tasks.title: The Python tutorial
tasks.description: The official tutorial — chapters on data structures are the ones analysts live in.

tasks.title: Kaggle Python course
tasks.description: Kaggle Learn's Python course, done in a notebook so you can run code as you go.

tasks.title: Loops, dicts & comprehensions
tasks.description: Write a script that reads a list of (name, score) pairs, keeps the top 3 in a dict, and prints a summary using one list comprehension.

nodes.title: Joins & Aggregations
nodes.description: Where the real power is: combining tables with JOIN and summarizing with GROUP BY.

tasks.title: Kaggle Learn: database relationships
tasks.description: Kaggle's course on working with related tables: joins, keys and one-to-many.

tasks.title: JOIN two tables
tasks.description: Find a two-table dataset (e.g. orders + customers). Write an INNER JOIN that returns order totals per customer, and a LEFT JOIN showing customers with zero orders.

tasks.title: GROUP BY + HAVING
tasks.description: From the same dataset: the top 5 categories by total amount, using GROUP BY and HAVING to keep only groups above a threshold you choose.

nodes.title: DataFrames with Pandas
nodes.description: The workhorse of Python data work: load, filter, transform and summarize tables fast.

tasks.title: The pandas user guide
tasks.description: The official docs' introductory sections: index, selection and aggregation.

tasks.title: Load, filter, summarize a CSV
tasks.description: Load a public CSV with pandas, filter to one condition, then produce the mean and max of a numeric column per category with one groupby call.

tasks.title: Pandas quiz
tasks.description: DataFrames, read_csv and groupby.

questions.prompt: A pandas DataFrame is best described as…
questions.explanation: A DataFrame is a labelled, columnar 2-D table; the 1-D version is a Series.

questions.prompt: Which method loads a CSV file into a DataFrame?
questions.explanation: pd.read_csv is the standard entry point; pandas also reads Excel, JSON, SQL and more.

options: One row per city with total sales
questions.explanation: groupby splits by the key column, applies the aggregation, and returns one row per group.

nodes.title: Data Cleaning
nodes.description: Where 80% of the job lives: missing values, bad types, duplicates and messy dates.

tasks.title: Handle missing values
tasks.description: On a dataset with missing data: report how many cells are missing per column, then fix them with an informed choice (drop, fill with the median, or a sentinel) and justify it in one sentence.

tasks.title: Fix types & duplicates
tasks.description: Convert a text column of numbers to numeric, coerce invalid dates, and remove fully duplicated rows. Print the row count before and after.

tasks.title: Normalize dates
tasks.description: Take a column with dates in mixed formats (e.g. 2024-01-05, 05/01/2024) and produce a single clean datetime column plus derived month and weekday columns.

nodes.title: Data Visualization
nodes.description: Show your findings honestly: the right chart for the right question, with labels and context.

tasks.title: Matplotlib guide
tasks.description: The official Matplotlib docs: figures, axes and the three chart types that do 80% of the work.

tasks.title: Kaggle Learn: data visualization
tasks.description: Kaggle's visualization course: line, bar and scatter charts with seaborn/matplotlib.

tasks.title: Three charts, one dataset
tasks.description: From one cleaned dataset, produce a line chart (trend over time), a bar chart (comparison across categories) and a scatter plot (relationship between two numbers). Title each and label the axes.

nodes.title: Statistics Essentials
nodes.description: The math that keeps you honest: distributions, central tendency, spread and when a result is real.

tasks.title: Kaggle Learn: data analysis (statistics)
tasks.description: Kaggle's statistics lessons: mean/median, distributions and basic inference.

tasks.title: Mean, median & distributions
tasks.description: Compute mean, median and standard deviation for one numeric column. Sketch (or plot) its distribution and write two sentences on whether the mean or the median better represents a 'typical' value.

tasks.title: Statistics quiz
tasks.description: Central tendency, spread and sampling.

questions.prompt: Which measure of center is least affected by extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The median splits the data in half, so one extreme value barely moves it; the mean is dragged along.
Standard deviation describes how far values typically sit from the mean.

options: Some groups are systematically over- or under-represented
questions.explanation: Bias means the sampling process consistently skews which people/data make it into the sample.

nodes.title: Dashboards & Reporting
nodes.description: Package your analysis for decisions: a dashboard someone else can read in under a minute.

tasks.title: Looker Studio help
tasks.description: The free dashboard tool's docs: connecting data, building charts and sharing reports.

tasks.title: Build a 4-metric dashboard
tasks.description: From a real dataset: one dashboard with exactly four metrics (e.g. total, trend, top-5 breakdown, comparison). Someone should get the story from the layout alone.

tasks.title: Public analysis report
tasks.description: Publish a small end-to-end analysis: a public dataset, your cleaning steps, three charts, and a five-sentence conclusion answering the question you started with. Host it anywhere (GitHub Pages, a notebook, a blog) and share the URL.
